findings.affected_surface: python_stdlib: sys.lazy_modules public attribute type changed from dict to set
findings.old_behavior: sys.lazy_modules was a dict mapping parent package names (str) to sets of submodule names (set[str]). Code could do dict operations: subscript access (sys.lazy_modules["pkg"]), .items(), .keys(), .values(), isinstance(..., dict) checks.
findings.new_behavior: sys.lazy_modules is a flat set of fully-qualified lazy module name strings (set[str]). Only set operations work: "pkg.sub" in sys.lazy_modules, iteration, len(), clear(). Dict subscript and dict-specific methods will raise TypeError.
findings.compatibility_reason: Per PEP 810, sys.lazy_modules is a documented public Python API exposed via the sys module. Changing from dict to set breaks any code that uses dict methods on this attribute — including subscript access, .items(), .keys(), .values(), and isinstance(..., dict) checks (which the patch's own test suite updates explicitly). All test assertions in Lib/test/test_lazy_import/__init__.py were updated from dict-style access to set membership checks, confirming this is a breaking behavioral change requiring test migration. The NEWS fragment (Misc/NEWS.d/next/Core_and_Builtins/2026-05-18-18-36-28.gh-issue-148587.-RD3z5.rst) documents this as a user-visible change.

evidence.snippet: ``sys.lazy_modules`` is now a set instead of a dict as initially spelled out in PEP 810.

findings.why_not_internal_only: sys.lazy_modules is a documented public Python API attribute on the sys module per PEP 810. It is directly observable by Python code and C extensions accessing sys module attributes. The type change from dict to set breaks the established public interface.
findings.uncertainty: None. The type change is explicit at the C implementation level (PyDict_New → PySet_New), documented in the NEWS fragment, and all test assertions were migrated.
findings.recommended_review: Verify that downstream code (stdlib, pip, setuptools, etc.) using sys.lazy_modules dict access is updated to use set membership checks.
findings.test_recommendation: Run Lib/test/test_lazy_import/__init__.py in its entirety on both before and after builds to confirm all assertions pass. Specifically test: (1) isinstance(sys.lazy_modules, set) passes, (2) isinstance(sys.lazy_modules, dict) fails, (3) 'module.name' in sys.lazy_modules works, (4) sys.lazy_modules['name'] raises TypeError, (5) len(), iteration, clear() work on the set.
